29020.e: Napoleon wanted to regain control of the rich colony. He sent a large army under General Leclerc.

29021.q: Where did Toussaint Louverture die in 1803?
29021.e: The French captured him in 1802 and took him to the Fort de Joux in the Jura, near the Swiss border. He died there of cold and illness.
29021.m: Toussaint Louverture died as a prisoner in France.

29022.q: Which decision did France make in 1794, partly because of the uprising in Saint-Domingue?
a: It abolished slavery in its colonies
It sold the colony to Spain
It declared war on the USA
29022.e: The French National Convention abolished slavery in all colonies in 1794.
29022.m: France abolished slavery for the first time in 1794.

29023.q: What title of honour does Simón Bolívar have?
29023.e: In South America Bolívar is honoured as “El Libertador”. He led many South American countries to independence.
29023.m: Simón Bolívar is called the Liberator.

29024.q: From which colonial power did Simón Bolívar free several countries in South America?
29024.e: Bolívar fought against Spanish rule in South America. Brazil, on the other hand, was a colony of Portugal.
29024.m: Bolívar fought against Spanish colonial rule.

29025.q: In which city was Simón Bolívar born in 1783?
29025.e: Bolívar was born in Caracas, today the capital of Venezuela. He came from a rich family.
29025.m: Simón Bolívar was born in Caracas.

29026.q: Which country is named after Simón Bolívar?
29026.e: Bolivia got its name in 1825 in honour of Bolívar. He was also the country's first president.
29026.m: Bolivia bears the name of Simón Bolívar.

29027.q: What was the large state that Bolívar founded in 1819 called?
29027.e: Gran Colombia covered roughly today's countries of Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador and Panama. The state broke up again in 1830/31.
29027.m: Bolívar dreamed of a large, united South America.

29028.q: What did Simón Bolívar promise when Haiti helped him in the fight against Spain?
a: To give Haiti lots of gold
29028.e: The Haitian president Alexandre Pétion gave Bolívar weapons and ships. In return Bolívar promised to abolish slavery in the liberated areas.
29028.m: Haiti helped Bolívar in the fight against Spain.

29029.q: What is Venezuela's currency, named after Simón Bolívar, called?
29029.e: Venezuela's currency is called the bolívar. Many squares and streets in South America also bear his name.

29030.q: When did most of the countries of South America become independent from Spain?
a: At the beginning of the 19th century
29030.e: Between about 1810 and 1825, Bolívar in the north and José de San Martín in the south fought against Spain. After that most South American countries were free.
29030.m: South America became independent at the beginning of the 19th century.

29031.q: In which years did the American Civil War take place?
29031.e: The Civil War began in April 1861 and ended in spring 1865. It is also known as the War of Secession.
29031.m: The American Civil War lasted from 1861 to 1865.

29032.q: Which two sides fought against each other in the American Civil War?
a: The Northern states and the Southern states
The East Coast and the West Coast
29032.e: The Northern states (the Union) fought against the Southern states that had broken away (the Confederacy). It was mainly about slavery.
29032.m: In the Civil War the North fought against the South.

29033.q: What did the Southern states that broke away call themselves?
29033.e: Eleven Southern states left the Union and founded the Confederate States of America. Their president was Jefferson Davis.
29033.m: The Southern states called themselves the Confederate States of America.

29034.q: Which side started the American Civil War in 1861 with an attack on a fort?
29034.e: In April 1861 troops of the Southern states fired on Fort Sumter in South Carolina. That was the start of the fighting.
29034.m: The Civil War began with an attack by the Southern states.

29035.q: Which battle of 1863 is seen as the turning point of the Civil War?
29035.e: At Gettysburg in Pennsylvania the Southern army was beaten in July 1863. After that the South could no longer push into the North.
29035.m: Gettysburg was the turning point of the Civil War.

29036.q: Who was the best-known general of the Southern states?
29036.e: Robert E. Lee led the most important army of the Confederacy. He was thought to be a very skilful commander.
29036.m: Robert E. Lee led the troops of the Southern states.

29037.q: Which general of the Northern states later became President of the USA?
29037.e: Ulysses S. Grant led the Union troops to victory. From 1869 to 1877 he was President of the USA.
29037.m: General Grant became president after the war.

29038.q: How did the American Civil War end in 1865?
a: The USA was split into two countries
29038.e: In April 1865 General Lee surrendered with the most important army of the Southern states. That practically ended the war.
29038.m: The North won the Civil War.

29039.q: Which number president of the USA was Abraham Lincoln?
29039.e: Lincoln was elected in 1860 and took office in 1861. He led the USA through the Civil War.
29039.m: Abraham Lincoln was the 16th president of the USA.

29040.q: Which party did Abraham Lincoln belong to?
29040.e: Lincoln was the first president from the Republican Party. It was against slavery spreading into new territories.

29041.q: What did Abraham Lincoln declare on 1 January 1863?
a: The slaves in the Southern states are free
The USA is independent from England
29041.e: With the Emancipation Proclamation Lincoln declared the slaves in the rebel Southern states free. But slavery was only completely abolished in 1865.
29041.m: In 1863 Lincoln declared the slaves in the South free.

29042.q: Which form of government did Lincoln describe with the words “government of the people, by the people, for the people”?
29042.e: Lincoln said these words in 1863 in his short speech at Gettysburg. In a democracy the people decide who governs.
29042.m: Lincoln described democracy as government of the people.

29043.q: How did Abraham Lincoln die in April 1865?
a: He was shot in a theatre
29043.e: A supporter of the Southern states shot Lincoln in Ford's Theatre in Washington. Lincoln died the next morning.

29044.q: Whose side was the man who shot Abraham Lincoln in 1865 on?
29044.e: The killer was an actor and a supporter of the Southern states. He was furious that the South had lost the Civil War.
29044.m: A supporter of the Southern states murdered Lincoln.

29045.q: Which war did Abraham Lincoln lead the USA through?
29045.e: From 1861 to 1865 the Northern states fought against the Southern states. Lincoln held the country together, and in the end slavery was abolished.
29045.m: Lincoln led the USA through the Civil War.

29046.e: Lincoln was thought to be especially honest, hence the nickname “Honest Abe”. He came from a humble background.

29047.q: What was banned throughout the USA in 1865 by an amendment to the Constitution?
29047.e: The 13th Amendment came into force in December 1865. Since then slavery has been banned throughout the USA.
29047.m: Slavery has been banned in the USA since 1865.

29048.q: What does the holiday Juneteenth on 19 June remember?
a: The freeing of the last slaves in Texas in 1865
The end of the gold rush
29048.e: On 19 June 1865 Union troops in Galveston, Texas, announced that the slaves were free. Since 2021 Juneteenth has been a national holiday.
29048.m: Juneteenth remembers the end of slavery in Texas.

29049.q: On which plantations in the south of the USA did especially many slaves work?
29049.e: Cotton was the most important export of the Southern states. Growing it depended on the work of millions of enslaved people.
29049.m: The cotton in the South was picked by slaves.

29050.q: Which novel by Harriet Beecher Stowe made many people aware of the suffering of slaves in 1852?
29050.e: “Uncle Tom's Cabin” was a huge success and strengthened opposition to slavery in the North. It was translated into many languages.

29051.q: What were people who demanded the abolition of slavery called?
29051.e: The word comes from “abolish”. Well-known abolitionists were Frederick Douglass and William Lloyd Garrison.

29052.q: Which former slave became a famous speaker and writer against slavery?
29052.e: Frederick Douglass escaped from slavery in 1838. His autobiography and his speeches made him world-famous.
29052.m: Frederick Douglass fought slavery with words.

29053.q: What was banned in the USA from 1808, although slavery continued?
a: Bringing in new slaves from Africa
29053.e: A law banned the import of slaves from 1808. But slaves continued to be sold within the USA.
29053.m: From 1808 no more slaves could be brought into the USA.

29054.q: What is Harriet Tubman famous for?
a: She helped many slaves to escape
She was the first female president of the USA
29054.e: Harriet Tubman escaped from slavery herself. After that she went back to the South several times and led others to freedom.
29054.m: Harriet Tubman led slaves to freedom.

29055.q: What was the secret network of escape routes and hiding places for slaves called?
29055.e: The Underground Railroad was not a real railway but a network of helpers and safe houses. It led to the Northern states and to Canada.
29055.m: The Underground Railroad was a secret escape network.

29056.q: Which nickname did Harriet Tubman get?
29056.e: Just as Moses in the Bible led his people out of slavery, Tubman led people to freedom. That is why she was called “Moses”.

29057.q: In which part of the USA was there mainly slavery until the Civil War?
29057.e: On the big plantations in the South enslaved people had to harvest cotton and tobacco. That is why many fled to the North.
29057.m: Slavery was mainly widespread in the Southern states.

29058.q: What job did Harriet Tubman take on in the Civil War?
a: She worked as a scout for the Northern states
She was a general of the Southern states
29058.e: Tubman served the Union as a scout, spy and nurse. In 1863 she helped with a raid that freed more than 700 slaves.
29058.m: Harriet Tubman helped the Union in the Civil War.

29059.q: How many people did Harriet Tubman personally lead to freedom on her roughly 13 rescue journeys?
29059.e: Tubman secretly went back to Maryland about 13 times and brought out about 70 people, including family members and friends. She gave exact instructions for escaping to another 50 to 60 people.
29059.m: Harriet Tubman herself rescued about 70 people from slavery.

29060.q: Where did many slaves flee to in order to be completely safe from their pursuers?
29060.e: A law of 1850 allowed escaped slaves to be caught even in the North of the USA. That is why Tubman led people all the way to Canada, where slavery was banned.
29060.m: Canada was a safe place for many who escaped.

29061.q: In which year was gold found in California, starting the gold rush?
29061.e: In January 1848 James W. Marshall found gold while building a sawmill. Soon hundreds of thousands of people poured into California.
29061.m: The California gold rush began in 1848.

29062.q: While building the sawmill of which Swiss emigrant was gold discovered in California in 1848?
29062.e: Johann August Sutter came from the area around Basel and founded the colony “New Helvetia” in California. The gold find brought him no luck: gold seekers took over his land and he became poor.
29062.m: The gold was found on the land of the Swiss Johann August Sutter.

29063.q: What were the gold seekers who came to California in 1849 called?
29063.e: Most gold seekers came in 1849, hence the name “Forty-Niners”. An American football team from San Francisco still has this name today.
29063.m: The gold seekers of 1849 were called Forty-Niners.

29064.q: Which city grew from a small place into a big city because of the gold rush?
29064.e: San Francisco was the most important port for the gold seekers. The city grew enormously within a few years.
29064.m: San Francisco grew big because of the gold rush.

29065.q: Which country did California belong to before it became part of the USA?
29065.e: Mexico handed California over to the USA in 1848. Because of all the gold seekers, it became a state as early as 1850.
29065.m: California used to belong to Mexico.

29066.q: Which simple method did many gold seekers use to look for gold in rivers?
29066.e: When panning for gold, you swirl sand and water in a pan. The heavy gold stays at the bottom.
29066.m: Gold seekers panned for gold in the sand.

29067.q: Who lost especially much land and many lives because of the gold rush?
a: The gold traders in New York
29067.e: Gold seekers drove out the Indigenous peoples, and many were killed by violence and disease. Their numbers fell sharply within a few decades.
29067.m: For the native peoples of California the gold rush was a catastrophe.

29068.q: What attracted many settlers to the west of the USA in the 19th century?
29068.e: With the Homestead Act of 1862 you were given about 65 hectares of land if you farmed it for five years. This attracted many settlers to the West.
29068.m: Free land attracted settlers to the West.

29069.q: In which year was the first transcontinental railway in the USA finished?
29069.e: On 10 May 1869 the tracks from east and west met at Promontory Summit in Utah. Now you could travel across the USA in a few days.
29069.m: Since 1869 a railway has connected the east and west coasts of the USA.

29070.q: What is the forced removal of the Cherokee in 1838, in which thousands died, called?
29070.e: The US government drove the Cherokee from their homeland in the south-east to what is now Oklahoma. On the way thousands died of cold, hunger and disease.
29070.m: The Trail of Tears was the expulsion of the Cherokee.

29071.q: Which battle did the Sioux and Cheyenne win against General Custer in 1876?
29071.e: At the Little Bighorn, warriors under Sitting Bull and Crazy Horse defeated George Custer's troops. Custer and all the soldiers under his direct command died.
29071.m: At the Little Bighorn the Sioux defeated Custer.

29072.q: Which animal was almost wiped out in the 19th century, taking away the livelihood of many prairie peoples?
29072.e: Hunters killed millions of bison until only a few hundred were left by around 1890. For the prairie peoples, bison meant food, clothing and materials.
29072.m: With the bison, the prairie peoples lost their livelihood.

29073.q: Where were many Native Americans forced to go in the 19th century?
29073.e: The US government forced many peoples to move to areas assigned to them. These reservations were often on poor land.
29073.m: Many Native Americans had to move to reservations.

29074.q: Which event of 1890 is seen as the end of the Indian Wars?
a: The building of the Panama Canal
29074.e: At Wounded Knee in South Dakota, US soldiers killed hundreds of Lakota, including many women and children. After that there was no more large armed resistance.
29074.m: Wounded Knee in 1890 marks the end of the Indian Wars.

29075.q: What was the long settlers' route called that led from Missouri to the Pacific coast in the north-west from the 1840s?
29075.e: Hundreds of thousands of settlers travelled about 3,500 kilometres west on the Oregon Trail in covered wagons. The journey usually took four to six months.
29075.m: Settlers travelled west along the Oregon Trail in covered wagons.

29076.q: What did France become after the February Revolution of 1848?
29076.e: In February 1848 the king in Paris was overthrown. France became a republic again.
29076.m: In 1848 France became a republic again.

29077.q: What did the Frankfurt National Assembly work out in 1848?
a: A constitution for all of Germany
29077.e: The first freely elected parliament for all of Germany met in St Paul's Church in Frankfurt. It wrote a constitution, but it never came into force.
29077.m: The Frankfurt National Assembly wrote a constitution for Germany.

29078.q: What did Louis Napoleon, Napoleon's nephew, call himself when he later became emperor?
29078.e: Louis Napoleon was elected President of France in 1848. In 1852 he made himself emperor as Napoleon III.
29078.m: Napoleon's nephew became emperor as Napoleon III.

29079.q: Which Austrian state chancellor had to resign and flee in March 1848?
29079.e: Since the Congress of Vienna, Metternich had stood for the suppression of liberal ideas. When the revolution broke out in Vienna, he resigned and fled to England.
29079.m: Metternich's flight in 1848 ended a whole era.

29080.q: What colours was the flag of the German revolutionaries of 1848?
29080.e: Black, red and gold was the symbol of unity and freedom. In March 1848 the German Confederation declared these colours its official colours.
29080.m: In 1848 black, red and gold stood for unity and freedom.

29081.q: What did the King of Prussia turn down in 1849?
a: The German imperial crown from the parliament
29081.e: The National Assembly offered King Frederick William IV the imperial crown. But he did not want a crown “from the hands of the people”.
29081.m: The Prussian king turned down the imperial crown in 1849.

29082.q: Which country became a federal state with a new federal constitution in 1848?
29082.e: After the Sonderbund War of 1847, Switzerland adopted a federal constitution on 12 September 1848. The confederation of states became a modern federal state.
29082.m: The Swiss federal state was created in 1848.

29083.q: What are the revolutions of 1848 in many European countries also called?
29083.e: In 1848 people in many countries rose up at the same time for freedom, constitutions and national unity. That is why people speak of the “Springtime of Nations”.
29083.m: The Springtime of Nations swept through large parts of Europe in 1848.

29084.q: What is the 1848 revolution in the German states called, after the month it broke out?
29084.e: In March 1848 there was great unrest in the German states. The princes had to appoint liberal “March ministers” and promise reforms.
29084.m: In Germany the revolution began in March 1848.

29085.q: Which state was founded in 1871 under the leadership of Otto von Bismarck?
29085.e: After the victory over France, the German Empire was founded in 1871. Bismarck became its first Chancellor.
29085.m: Bismarck founded the German Empire in 1871.

29086.q: Which nickname did Otto von Bismarck get?
29086.e: Because of his hard and determined politics he was called the “Iron Chancellor”. The name also refers to his speech about “iron and blood”.
29086.m: Bismarck is known as the “Iron Chancellor”.

29087.q: According to Bismarck's famous speech of 1862, how would the great questions of the day be decided?
29087.e: Bismarck said that the great questions would not be decided by speeches and majority votes, but by “iron and blood”. He meant weapons and war.
29087.m: Bismarck relied on “iron and blood” rather than speeches in parliament.

29088.q: Which office did Otto von Bismarck hold in the German Empire?
29088.e: Bismarck was the first Imperial Chancellor from 1871 to 1890. He led the government, and the emperor stood above him.
29088.m: Bismarck was the first German Chancellor.

29089.q: Which political movement was Bismarck's law of 1878 aimed against?
29089.e: The so-called Anti-Socialist Law banned social democratic clubs, meetings and newspapers. It applied until 1890.
29089.m: With the Anti-Socialist Law Bismarck fought the Social Democrats.

29090.q: What is Bismarck's conflict with the Catholic Church in the 1870s called?
29090.e: In the Kulturkampf Bismarck wanted to push back the influence of the Catholic Church. At that time civil marriage at the registry office was introduced, for example.
29090.m: The Kulturkampf was a conflict between Bismarck and the Catholic Church.

29091.q: Which emperor dismissed Otto von Bismarck in 1890?
29091.e: The young emperor wanted to rule himself and quarrelled with the old chancellor. In 1890 Bismarck had to hand in his resignation.

29092.q: What was the parliament of the German Empire, elected by men, called?
29092.e: The Reichstag was elected by universal and equal suffrage for men aged 25 and over. It passed laws and the budget.
29092.m: In the German Empire men elected the Reichstag.

29093.q: Who became the first emperor of the German Empire in 1871?
29093.e: The King of Prussia was proclaimed German Emperor. He reigned until his death in 1888.
29093.m: The Prussian king Wilhelm I became the first German Emperor.

29094.q: Which war came immediately before the founding of the German Empire in 1871?
29094.e: In the war of 1870/71 the German states fought together against France. The shared victory made the founding of the Empire possible.
29094.m: The war against France in 1870/71 led to the founding of the Empire.

29095.q: Which territory did France have to give up to the German Empire in 1871?
29095.e: In the Treaty of Frankfurt in 1871 France lost Alsace and part of Lorraine. This loss strained relations between the two countries for decades.

29096.q: Which Prussian politician is seen as the founder of the German Empire of 1871?
29096.e: Otto von Bismarck was Prime Minister of Prussia. With wars against Denmark, Austria and France he prepared the unification of Germany.
29096.m: Bismarck is seen as the founder of the German Empire.

29098.q: In which palace was the King of Prussia proclaimed German Emperor in 1871?
29098.e: The proclamation took place in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles near Paris, while the war against France was still going on. The French felt this was a humiliation.
29098.m: The German Empire was proclaimed at Versailles in 1871.

29099.q: Which German state led the unification of Germany in 1871?
29099.e: Prussia was the largest and strongest German state. Under its leadership first the North German Confederation and then, in 1871, the German Empire were created.
29099.m: Prussia led the unification of Germany.

29100.q: On which island did Garibaldi land in 1860 with the “Expedition of the Thousand”?
29100.e: Garibaldi landed near Marsala with about a thousand volunteers. He conquered Sicily and then southern Italy.
29100.m: The Expedition of the Thousand began in Sicily in 1860.

29101.q: What were Garibaldi's volunteers called because of their clothes?
29101.e: The fighters wore red shirts, which became their sign. They became the symbol of Italian unification.

29102.q: What did Giuseppe Garibaldi fight for?
29102.e: For a long time Italy was made up of many separate states. Garibaldi fought for them to become one country, and in 1861 the Kingdom of Italy was created.
29102.m: Garibaldi is a hero of Italian unification.

29103.q: On which continent did Garibaldi fight before he returned to Italy in 1848?
29103.e: Garibaldi lived in exile for years and fought in Brazil and Uruguay. That is why he is also called the “Hero of the Two Worlds”.
29103.m: Garibaldi is known as the “Hero of the Two Worlds”.

29104.q: Which state was created in 1861 through the Risorgimento?
29104.e: The Kingdom of Italy was created out of many small states in 1861. Victor Emmanuel II became its first king.
29104.m: The Kingdom of Italy was founded in 1861.

29105.q: Which freedom fighter conquered the south of Italy with his Redshirts for unification?
29105.e: In 1860 Garibaldi conquered Sicily and southern Italy with about a thousand volunteers. Then he handed the territories over to the King of Sardinia-Piedmont.
29105.m: Garibaldi was a hero of Italian unification.

29106.q: What is the 19th-century Italian unification movement called?
29106.e: The word means “rising again”. It refers to the path from many small states to one Italian nation state.
29106.m: The Risorgimento led to the unification of Italy.

29107.q: Which city became the capital after the unification of Italy?
29107.e: In 1870 Italian troops marched into Rome. From 1871 Rome was the capital of the Kingdom of Italy.
29107.m: Rome became the capital of united Italy.

29108.q: Which organisation did Henry Dunant suggest after seeing the wounded of the Battle of Solferino in 1859?
29108.e: Henry Dunant from Geneva saw the misery of the wounded after the battle in northern Italy. He proposed the founding of the Red Cross, which was set up in 1863.
29108.m: After Solferino, Henry Dunant proposed the Red Cross.

29109.q: Roughly how long did Queen Victoria reign?
29109.e: Victoria became queen in 1837 at the age of 18 and reigned until 1901, more than 63 years. That was longer than any British ruler before her.
29109.m: Queen Victoria reigned for over 60 years.

29110.q: What was the name of Queen Victoria's husband?
29110.e: Victoria married her cousin Albert in 1840. He was an important adviser. After his death in 1861 she wore mourning clothes for decades.

29111.q: Which great empire did Queen Victoria rule over?
29111.e: In Queen Victoria's time the British Empire was bigger than ever before. It included territories on every continent.
29111.m: Victoria ruled over the British Empire.

29112.q: What is the period of her reign called?
29112.e: The period was marked by industrialisation, strict moral ideas and the greatest extent of the British Empire.
29112.m: The Victorian era is named after Queen Victoria.

29113.q: Which extra title did Queen Victoria hold from 1876?
29113.e: In 1876 Prime Minister Benjamin Disraeli had Victoria given the title “Empress of India”. It was meant to stress the importance of the most valuable colony.
29113.m: From 1876 Queen Victoria was also Empress of India.

29114.q: How many children did Queen Victoria have?
29114.e: Victoria had nine children. Many of them married into European royal families, which is why Victoria is called the “grandmother of Europe”.
29114.m: Victoria is called the “grandmother of Europe”.

29115.q: Around what time did Queen Victoria die?
29115.e: Victoria died in January 1901 on the Isle of Wight. The 20th century had just begun.

29116.q: Who became king after Queen Victoria's death?
29116.e: Her eldest son became king as Edward VII. He was already almost 60 years old. Her husband Albert had died back in 1861.

29117.q: Who did Karl Marx write the Communist Manifesto with?
29117.e: Engels was a close friend of Marx and wrote many works with him. As the son of a factory owner, he also supported Marx with money.
29117.m: Marx and Engels wrote the Manifesto together.

29118.q: In which year was the Communist Manifesto published?
29118.e: It was published in February 1848, shortly before several revolutions broke out. At first hardly anyone noticed it, but later it was translated into many languages.
29118.m: The Communist Manifesto was published in 1848.

29119.q: What did Marx and Engels demand in the Communist Manifesto?
a: Factories and machines should belong to everyone
Every family should own its own factory
29119.e: Marx and Engels wanted the means of production to belong not to a few rich people but to the whole of society. The workers were to unite for this.
29119.m: In the Manifesto, factories were to belong to everyone.

29120.q: According to the first sentence of the Manifesto, which “spectre” is haunting Europe?
29120.e: The Manifesto begins with the sentence “A spectre is haunting Europe, the spectre of communism.” Marx and Engels meant the fear of the powerful.
29120.m: The Manifesto begins with the spectre of communism.

29121.q: In Marx's writings, what is the class that owns the factories and machines called?
29121.e: The bourgeoisie owns the means of production. According to Marx, it is in a class struggle against the workers.
29121.m: In Marx's view the bourgeoisie owns the means of production.

29122.q: Which job did Karl Marx do besides his work as a thinker?
29122.e: Marx wrote for newspapers and in 1848/49 even ran a newspaper in Cologne. He earned part of his living by writing.
29122.m: Karl Marx also worked as a journalist.

29123.q: Which country did Karl Marx come from?
29123.e: Marx was born in Trier in 1818. Later he lived in exile, mainly in London.
